id: qc-09
title: Logical neutral-atom processor
paper: Bluvstein et al., Logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays (arXiv Dec 2023; Nature 626, 58, 2024)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03982
type: Replication
cutoff: 2023-12-07
domain: qc
profile: hardware-milestone

## expected_verdict
Supported (scoped), tier C. A programmable neutral-atom processor runs logical circuits on up to 280 physical / 48 logical qubits. The largest algorithmic gains (XEB, GHZ fidelity) come from error detection with postselection, at a cost in discarded runs. That is not active fault-tolerant correction. No independent replication. Directly relevant to the Q-Factor neutral-atom track.

## I0
Can encoded neutral-atom circuits improve task fidelity over physical-qubit implementations?

## evidence
- Platform: Rb atoms, up to 280 physical qubits, zoned architecture (entangling / storage / readout), AOD atom transport, Rydberg gates (99.5% two-qubit fidelity), mid-circuit readout, feedforward.
- Surface code: transversal CNOT between two codes; two-qubit logic gate improves as d goes 3 → 5 → 7, using correlated decoding (Fig. 2).
- Color codes (d = 3): break-even state preparation; fault-tolerant 4-logical GHZ at 72(2)% fidelity; 99.85% with full postselection on stabilizers; discarding 50% of runs gives 90% (Fig. 3d); up to 40 color codes operated.
- [[8,3,2]] blocks: IQP-type sampling circuits with up to 48 logical qubits, 228 logical two-qubit gates, 48 logical CCZs; logical XEB finite and improving with error detection; outperforms physical-qubit upper bounds (Fig. 4–5).
- Fast-scrambling simulation with logical qubits also beats physical encodings.

## intake
- Scope: encoded logical circuits on neutral atoms outperform physical-qubit circuits on specific tasks (GHZ, XEB sampling, scrambling), plus surface-code gate improvement with distance.
- Regime: shallow logical circuits; error detection with sliding-scale postselection; [[8,3,2]] codes (distance 2, detection only) for the 48-logical runs.
- Assumptions: postselection overhead is acceptable for the task; physical comparators run comparable circuits; correlated decoding is valid.
- Falsifiers: gains vanish once discarded shots are charged (e.g. time-to-solution); or physical-qubit baselines were weaker than achievable.

## screen
- Must flag: [[8,3,2]] is an error-detecting code; headline fidelities depend on postselection acceptance; surface-code improvement is for one transversal gate, not deep computation.
- Must request: acceptance rates for every headline number; resource counts including discarded shots.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Bluvstein et al. 2022 coherent transport of entangled atom arrays; Evered et al. 2023 high-fidelity parallel Rydberg gates; Google 2023 surface-code scaling; [[8,3,2]] code (Campbell / Vasmer); IQP / hypercube sampling.
- Current mode: none independent in the inventory.

## designer
- Compare logical vs physical circuits at matched tasks; report fidelity and acceptance rate; compute effective throughput (fidelity × accepted fraction / time); separate detection-only from correction results.

## champion
- Best physical-qubit implementation of the same circuits on the same hardware, with error mitigation, charged the same shot budget.

## panel
- Accept with scope; require every postselected result to state its accepted fraction.

## run
- Stim simulation of the [[8,3,2]] sampling circuit at reported physical error rates: logical XEB vs acceptance. Hardware BLOCKED.

## verdict
- Label: Supported (scoped), tier C.
- Must say: detection + postselection drives the largest gains; surface-code gate improvement with distance is genuine; no independent replication.
- Must not say: fault-tolerant quantum computation achieved; or postselected fidelities equal corrected fidelities.

## audit
- Check: 280 physical / 48 logical; 228 two-qubit + 48 CCZ logical gates; GHZ 72(2)% vs 99.85% postselected; 90% at 50% acceptance; 99.5% physical CZ fidelity.

## variants
- Lower postselection cost or active correction on neutral atoms (deeper surface-code circuits with repeated rounds); relevant hardware question for our neutral-atom partnership track.
